It’ll make building simple functions significantly easier as you can just ask an AI to do it and it’s done. As opposed to building it yourself then having to look through page after page to figure out why your code doesn’t work. But you still need a programmer to put together these AI generated passages, and to debug them. Also it’s important to recognise that these AI’s are language models. They don’t understand the code at all, but they’re looking through millions of stackoverflow questions and answers and building a connection between them. So rather than asking stackoverflow a question, you ask it to an AI and that AI will generate a generic response from the culmination of millions of people’s work. But you still need that work in the first place. If a new library comes out, you need the AI to be trained on it with a significant amount of examples and that would take a very long time. So for anything remotely complicated or new, a literal dictionary isn’t going to be able to solve it.

Whether or not AI productivity gains compounds is an interesting question. I think it compounds if you use it in a way where you become more competent faster. You have instant access to expert opinion, instant access to great summaries of any field of information. An on demand peer to bounce an approach off of. Leveraging that means you hit the ground going fast and don’t waste time getting stuck and searching for information. On the contrary I think using it to “do the work plz” is negatively compounding. By yielding all thinking you degrade your own skills over time. Two paths with AI: an augment to accelerate your own competency, or a crutch insidiously eroding your brainpower through lack of use

My job can never be replaced by AI, because my job is whatever i want to do. I am, and will always be, doing my own thing, going trough life my way. AI is just one more step towards the post scarcity world that we have been approaching over the course of the last hundred years or so. The world right now is in such a way where i am allowed to do whatever i want (as long as "whatever i want" is productive), and sooner rather then later, my situation will become the standard, where we as people will have to decide if we will chase wealth or self actualization. Life is no longer like it was 200 years ago, where you did what your father did, and your life was already set out ahead of you the day you were born. Now we all must choose what to spend our lives on, do you want to be an engineer, a teacher or a plumber? And the amount of jobs have increased as the productivity of the already existing jobs had increased. We will never come to a point where all our jobs will be taken by AI, because we will just make more. Now the world we live in will change, but if it is better or worse, only time will tell. But i hope it gets better.
